title: How recursion unwinds: factorial of 4
goal: Trace a recursive function by hand and see how the call stack builds up and unwinds.

steps.narration: You flagged the call stack as shaky, so we will start there. Think of it as a pile of sticky notes. The newest note goes on top, and you always finish the top note first.

visual.content: Call stack = pile of notes, newest on top

steps.narration: Now the problem. Factorial of 4 means 4 times 3 times 2 times 1. A recursive function solves it by asking a smaller version of itself.
A smaller question every time has to stop somewhere. That stopping point is the base case. For factorial, one factorial is just one.
steps.checkpoint: Why do we need a base case at all?

steps.narration: Let's build the stack. We call factorial of 4. It cannot finish yet, so it waits for factorial of 3, which waits for 2, which waits for 1.

visual.content: f(4) waits on f(3) waits on f(2) waits on f(1)

steps.narration: Here is the base case answering. f of 1 returns 1. That is the top note, so it gets finished first.
steps.checkpoint: Which call finishes first, f(4) or f(1)?

steps.narration: Now the stack unwinds. f of 2 is 2 times 1, which is 2. Then f of 3 is 3 times 2, which is 6.
Finally f of 4 is 4 times 6. The answer is 24.

commonMistake: Forgetting the base case, so the function keeps calling itself and the stack never stops growing.
